transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brought me in today is that I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is staying seated. I'm a secondary school teacher, so I'm used to being on my feet a lot during the day, but this happens when I'm supposed to be sitting still. 

I'll just... suddenly need to go refill my coffee, or check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. Nothing is ever really urgent, but I just find myself getting out of my chair anyway.
Do you find yourself needing to get up or move around even in situations where you're not teaching, like at home or in meetings?

Yes, exactly. Like I was just saying, that's really the main issue. It happens in staff meetings, or even at home sitting at the dinner table. 

Everyone else will be staying in their seats, and I'll just... get up. I'll go grab more coffee, or look for a paper, or just stand at the back of the room. There's never a real reason or urgency for it, I just find it really hard to stay seated when I'm supposed to.
Do you feel restless or have a strong urge to move when you're sitting for a long time, and does moving around help relieve that feeling?

Yes, I do. Even if I manage to stay in my chair, I still feel that restlessness. Like when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or if I'm in church... I'll catch myself tapping my foot, or clicking my pen over and over. I just end up shifting around in my seat so much that I actually have to remind myself to settle down. So, moving definitely relieves that feeling, even if it's just those small movements while I'm trying to sit still.
